title: Cross-functional observability onboarding for new models
content:
Purpose:
This is a pragmatic, cross-team checklist and lightweight spec to onboard a new model (open or internal) into Redwood's production observability surface. Aim: minimum safe signals for rollout + clear owner handoffs so rollouts (canary/gradual) have actionable telemetry from day 0.

Audience:
- Applied ML: model behavior expectations, example artifact hooks.
- Serving/runtime engineers: tracing and span contract.
- Observability: dashboards, SLOs, sampling.
- SRE/Oncall: runbook pointers and alert gates.

High-level approach (one-pager):
1) Instrument minimal metrics during integration: request counts, token latency quantiles, error counts, cache warmness.
2) Add trace anchors for request->inference->kv operations and model fallback routing.
3) Create a compact dashboard template (canary + full traffic views).
4) Define SLIs/SLOs and rollout abort thresholds.
5) Post-launch: add quality signals (eval set replay) to detect hallucination/regression.

Minimum metrics (definitions):
- model.request.count: counter per model, tags: env, region, route, model_version, tenant_id
- model.request.errors: counter (http 5xx, inference failures, timeouts) with same tags
- model.token.latency.ms.p50/p95/p99: distribution summary sample per request (measured at token emit)
- model.end_to_end.latency.ms: time from ingress request received to last token sent (wall clock)
- kv_cache.hit_ratio: ratio = hits / (hits + misses) sampled per model/version, also track kv_cache.evictions_per_min
- batch.size.distribution: histogram of batch sizes (0..N) and batch.wait_ms.quantiles
- in_flight.requests: gauge of concurrent requests against model pool
- billing.tokens.generated: counter tagged by model_version and route (for cost attribution)

Tracing conventions (span & attribute guide):
- Root span: op_name = "http.request" (existing ingress).
- Inference span: op_name = "model.inference"; attributes: model.name, model.version, seq_len, tenant.id (if available), protocol (sync/stream).
- KV span(s): op_name = "kvcache.lookup" or "kvcache.write"; attributes: cache.key_hint (redact PI), cache.hit boolean, shard_id.
- Batch assembly span: op_name = "batcher.combine"; attributes: batch.size, wait_ms, schedule_policy.
- Router span for fallback: op_name = "router.resolve"; attributes: route.decision, fallback_reason.
- Correlation: trace_id propagated to logs via trace_id tag. Ensure request_id and trace_id are present on every log line.
- Sampling: default adaptive sampling 1% for cold-models, 5% for canary traffic, 20% for traffic producing errors or high latencies. Increase sampling for rollouts to 50% for first 24h if possible.
- Privacy redaction: never include raw prompt text or PHI in spans; include prompt_hash (sha256 truncated) if needed for correlation.

Dashboard/Panel checklist (compact two-tier template):
Tier A (canary + alerting):
- Canary request rate (model.request.count) with canary vs baseline overlay, 1m, 5m windows
- Errors (model.request.errors) absolute + rate per 1000 requests
- End-to-end latency p95 and p99, anomaly band compared to baseline
- KV hit ratio trend and banner if < threshold for 10m
- Rollout abort gauge: percent of traffic on canary, and automatic gate if error_rate > X or p99 latency increases > Y

Tier B (investigation panels):
- Token latency distribution heatmap by seq_len buckets
- Batch size histogram + throughput correlation panel (throughput vs batch_size)
- Trace samples: link to sampled traces filtered by model.inference spans > 500ms or errors
- Tenant-level cost attribution (billing.tokens.generated) and top-10 tenants by tokens
- Overlay: model version comparison (multiple series)

SLI/SLO suggestions (starter):
- Availability SLI: success_rate = 1 - model.request.errors / model.request.count ; SLO target: 99.9% for GA models, 99.0% for canaries
- Latency SLI: p95_end_to_end < 500ms; SLO depends on class (realtime vs batch)
- KV warmness SLI: kv_cache.hit_ratio > 0.75 for steady-state workloads

Rollout gates (automated canary aborts):
- Absolute error count increase > 2x baseline in 5m window AND error_rate > 0.1%
- p99 latency increase > 2x baseline OR p95 increase > 30% for 10m window
- KV hit ratio drop > 20% causing > 15% cost increase projection
(These thresholds are suggested defaults; product/solutions may tune per-customer.)

Instrumentation checklist (engineers):
- [ ] Add model.* metrics and ensure tags match conventions
- [ ] Emit model.inference spans with required attributes
- [ ] Expose batcher metrics and set histograms with consistent buckets
- [ ] Wire trace_id -> logs and set log sampling rules for high-volume tenants
- [ ] Add canary label or metadata to requests routed to canary variant
- [ ] Add token-level latency sampling (1 in 100 requests) for heatmap generation
- [ ] Create dashboard from observability/template-new-model (see linked artifacts)

Owner matrix (first-pass):
- Applied ML: define expected quality regressions, provide eval prompt set and baseline metrics. Owner: Ethan Morales
- Serving/runtime: implement spans & batcher metrics, ensure tag schema. Owner: Jonah Reed
- Observability product: dashboard templates, SLOs, alert rules. Owner: Priya Desai
- SRE: canary abort orchestration & Pager runbook. Owner: Asha Kaur

Post-launch signals to add after 1wk of steady traffic:
- Output-quality eval telemetry (eval replays, n-gram overlap, and hallucination checks)
- Token-level burst detection (identify spikes caused by long completions)
- Prompts distribution sketch (top prompt hashes) for drift detection

Quick queries (examples to put into dashboard data source):
- Errors per minute for model X: SELECT count(*) FROM metrics WHERE metric='model.request.errors' AND model='X' AND time > now()-5m GROUP BY time(1m)
- p95 token latency: SELECT percentile(token_latency_ms,95) FROM metrics WHERE model='X' AND time>now()-15m

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to reliably correlate eval-replay requests with production traces without leaking prompt content? (proposal: use prompt_hash and a private eval_id mapping)
- Multi-model fanout traces: should we attach all child spans to a single trace or separate traces per candidate? (ops prefers single trace for easier root-cause)
- Cost of high sampling during rollouts for extremely high-traffic customers — need budget guardrails

Notes to self / informal:
- Keep dashboard compact: one line per metric with clear color semantics (canary=orange, baseline=blue, alert=red).
- Ship a template and a tiny runbook for oncall to avoid frantic Slack threads on day 0.

If you're picking this up: run through the checklist with owners above, add any customer-specific thresholds to the rollout ticket, and ping #obs-oncall before enabling 50% sampling for a canary.

Revision history:
- 2025-06-05 initial draft by Priya
- 2025-06-12 updated sampling recommendations after call with SRE
- 2025-06-18 added owner matrix and quick queries
